basis: Peptide metabolic defect with skin ulcers and immune dysfunction; hearing loss 80-99%. Cap excludes cytopenias/splenomegaly (~65-75%) and hepatic, dental, skeletal and ocular findings.

decisions.haematologic: none: cytopenias in 3/4 and splenomegaly in 15/23 qualify, but the cap favors defining metabolic, skin and immune disease plus hearing loss in 80-99%.
decisions.infectious_immune: primary: immune dysfunction is frequent (80-99%), with recurrent infections in 4/4; this supports an intrinsic immune disorder.

basis: Spinal gray-matter injury defines AFM. Viral associations do not establish an infectious or autoimmune mechanism for the entire syndrome.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: AFM is defined as a spinal cord syndrome without an established cause; infection or autoimmunity is not required.

basis: Neurologic impairment and skin/hair pigment abnormalities define disease. Persistent refractive dysfunction from myopia occurs in 30-79%; optic atrophy and macular dystrophy occur in 5-29%.

decisions.ocular: involved: syndrome-associated myopia causes persistent ocular functional impairment in 30-79%; optic atrophy and macular dystrophy alone would fall below threshold.

basis: Tumor originates in the pineal endocrine gland within the CNS. Gaze and visual-field abnormalities reflect central pathway effects; direct ocular damage is not established.

decisions.ocular: none: gaze palsy and visual-field defects can arise from central compression or hydrocephalus; these annotations do not establish direct eye or optic-nerve damage.

basis: SCID with developmental delay 2/2, alopecia/erythroderma 1/1 and sensorineural hearing loss 1/2. Enamel hypoplasia 1/2 omitted at cap; bronchiectasis follows separate infections.

decisions.pulmonary: none: bronchiectasis in 1/2 is downstream of recurrent respiratory infections, separately diagnosed diseases promoted by the immunodeficiency.
decisions.otologic: involved: sensorineural hearing impairment in 1/2 patients supports persistent hearing loss above the 30% threshold, although the sample is very small.

basis: Respiratory disease, cataracts and malabsorption define the syndrome; progressive end-stage renal disease affected both reported siblings. Otitis omitted at cap.

decisions.ocular: primary: cataracts are a defining structural manifestation; retained within the cap alongside respiratory, intestinal and severe renal disease.
decisions.infectious_immune: none: recurrent infections do not establish an intrinsic immunodeficiency; the syndrome itself is not an infection. Four defining or severe organ manifestations take priority.

basis: Congenital GSD IV causes storage myopathy; dilated cardiomyopathy is characteristic and commonly reported (estimated >=30%). Respiratory failure reflects muscle weakness.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: dilated cardiomyopathy is characteristic and common in the congenital neuromuscular subtype (estimated >=30%); the exact frequency is uncertain.

basis: Intestinal enteroendocrine-cell deficiency defines digestive and endocrine dysfunction. Diabetes is not needed to justify the endocrine axis; hepatic injury may follow parenteral nutrition.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: defining absence of intestinal hormone-producing enteroendocrine cells is intrinsic endocrine dysfunction, independently of separately diagnosed diabetes.

basis: Paranasal sinus mucosal inflammation belongs to the pulmonary axis. The umbrella definition does not establish infection or a specific immune-mediated mechanism.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: sinusitis encompasses infectious and noninfectious inflammation; inflammation alone does not establish an infectious, autoimmune or immune-mediated disease.

basis: Spastic paraplegia, auditory hearing loss and symptomatic hiatal hernia define SPG29. Structural pes cavus occurs in 30-79%; bilirubin elevation alone does not establish hepatic damage.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: symptomatic hiatal or paraesophageal hernia is part of the syndrome's definition; hiatus hernia is annotated in 30-79%.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: fixed structural pes cavus occurs in 30-79%; this is musculoskeletal deformity within the syndrome, beyond weakness or spasticity alone.
decisions.otologic: primary: hearing impairment from auditory neuropathy is a defining manifestation; hearing loss belongs to the otologic axis and occurs in 30-79%.
